description:
Sleep Music | 3 Hours of Bansuri Flute | Indian Classical

Some nights your body is exhausted but your mind hasn't gotten the message yet.

You lie down. The room is quiet. But something keeps running — replaying the day, jumping to tomorrow, refusing to let the weight of the mattress mean anything. You don't need more noise. You need something to fill the silence in a way that gradually pulls the mind down with it.

This is 3 full hours of Bansuri — the Indian bamboo flute — in Raga Darbari Kanada. Darbari is a deep-midnight raga. Its phrases are slow, heavy, serious in a way that doesn't feel heavy to listen to. It doesn't ask anything of you. It just deepens, note by note, the way night deepens if you let it.

Three hours means you won't wake up when it ends. It plays through your whole sleep cycle and keeps going — no startling silence at the 90-minute mark.

A gentle Delta wave layer sits underneath at very low volume. Not there to do anything dramatic — just to keep the body moving in the direction of deep sleep.

🎵 What you'll hear:
- Bansuri — warm bamboo flute, breath-driven, unhurried
- Sparse phrases with long natural silences between them
- Very slow tempo — the music breathes slower than you will
- A barely-there low-frequency layer underneath (Delta, 2Hz)
- Unbroken three hours — no restarts, no transitions

⏱ Chapters
0:00   Settling in
20:00  First heaviness
45:00  Mind letting go
90:00  Deep sleep zone
150:00 Staying under
170:00 Peaceful close

🧠 How to use:
Press play before you're fully tired. Let it start before you need it. Phone face-down. Volume low but audible — you want to feel the music without it keeping you awake. Let it carry you the rest of the way down.

⏱ Best for:
• Mind that won't stop at night
• Trouble falling or staying asleep
• 1am to 4am wakeups
• Full night of unbroken sleep
• Background for deep rest

thumbnail_prompt: Pichwai/Kangra miniature painting style, ornate deep-indigo-and-gold patterned border with subtle crescent moon and night-bloom motifs, aged warm parchment background, deep-night palette (midnight indigo fading to soft black, single oil lamp glow casting warm amber light). Central figure: serene musician in deep-blue-and-cream attire seated on a low woven mat playing bansuri (long bamboo flute held horizontally to lips) in a quiet open-air night courtyard. Moonlight above, a single lotus pool or small water feature catching the light. The scene feels very still — no wind, no movement, just deep quiet. A low sleeping figure visible in soft background. Bold dark-teal serif overlay text reading 'SLEEP DEEPLY' top-center, traditional Devanagari-influenced serif typography, high contrast for mobile readability. Midnight-indigo and warm amber palette, deep still night mood, single composed scene, no clutter.
suno_prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals. Slow bansuri solo in raga Darbari Kanada, deep midnight sleep mood, very sparse breath-driven melodic flow with extremely long sustained notes and long silences between phrases, no percussion, no tabla, 432Hz tuning, 40-50 BPM very slow dreamy tempo, deep low-mid register (warm and heavy, not bright or high-pitched), cinematic deeply meditative production, hypnotic and grounding, suitable for extended looping in post-production, begins immediately with bansuri already playing at low volume, full sonic presence from first note. CRITICAL: Darbari Kanada uses komal Ga, komal Dha, komal Ni — the flat intervals give it natural weight and gravity. Emotionally: like consciousness sinking through layers — not dramatic, just inevitable. Very long meends (glides between notes). Low register, warm, heavy, patient. Each phrase completes before the next begins. 10-15 seconds of near-silence between phrases is correct. Delta wave layer at -22dB barely audible underneath. Bansuri mid-LOW register only — high bansuri is alerting not sleep-inducing.

production_spec.loop_seam: 10s in / 30s out, Suno extend 4-6x → loop in post to fill 180 min
production_spec.notes: Raga Darbari Kanada — deep midnight raga. Sa Re Ga(komal) Ma Pa Dha(komal) Ni(komal) Sa. The komal (flat) intervals create its characteristic heaviness. CRITICAL: First Suno clip must feel genuinely drowsy in low-mid register before you extend — if clip sounds bright or fast, regenerate with stronger low-register instruction. EMOTIONAL TAG ROTATION: clip 1: 'like consciousness sinking — heavy and inevitable' · clip 2: 'still and deep, like the middle of a silent night' · clip 3: 'like the last thought before sleep, fading'. Mix: Bansuri -3dB (quiet main), Binaural -22dB (barely audible), LUFS -16dB (sleep audience, quieter than standard -14 ships). 3hr = 4-6 Suno clips + loop extension in post. Seam at 10s in, fade out at 30s out for clean loop.
